_about: Disease -> mechanism links curated for the demo. Every quote must appear verbatim in the PubMed abstract of its PMID; enrich.py fetches the abstract and drops any row whose quote does not match. Curation was AI-assisted and has not been checked by a domain expert yet, so the UI labels these 'AI-curated, quote verified'.

MECH:loss_of_function.name: Loss of function
MECH:loss_of_function.description: The variant reduces or abolishes what the protein normally does (including haploinsufficiency: one working copy is not enough).

MECH:gain_of_function.name: Gain of function
MECH:gain_of_function.description: The variant makes the protein more active than normal or gives it a new, harmful activity.

MECH:nmda_receptor_dysfunction.name: NMDA receptor dysfunction
MECH:nmda_receptor_dysfunction.description: Altered activity of the NMDA-type glutamate receptor, a channel that lets calcium and sodium into neurons when glutamate binds.

MECH:sodium_channel_dysfunction.name: Sodium channel dysfunction (Nav1.1)
MECH:sodium_channel_dysfunction.description: Reduced function of the Nav1.1 sodium channel that inhibitory (GABAergic) neurons need to fire.

MECH:impaired_neurotransmitter_release.name: Impaired neurotransmitter release
MECH:impaired_neurotransmitter_release.description: Synaptic vesicles release less neurotransmitter, so communication between neurons is weakened.

MECH:kinase_signalling_loss.name: Loss of kinase signalling
MECH:kinase_signalling_loss.description: Loss of an enzyme that adds phosphate groups to other proteins, disrupting the signalling pathways it controls.

CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD, DEE2), one of the most common genetic epilepsies, is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the brain-enriched kinase CDKL5.
Because CDKL5 mutations identified in patients with CDD cause enzymatic loss of function, CDKL5 catalytic activity is likely strongly associated with the disease.
Dravet syndrome is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by heterozygous, loss-of-function, pathogenic variants in the SCN1A gene.

SCN1A encodes for the alpha subunit of the voltage-gated type I sodium channel (NaV1.1), the primary voltage-gated sodium channel responsible for generation of action potentials in GABAergic inhibitory interneurons.
